artifacts.title: Rewrite enable/disable logic
artifacts.body:
Rewrite enable/disable logic

#### PR checklist

- [ ] Addresses an existing issue: #0000
- [ ] New feature, bugfix, or enhancement
  - [X] Includes tests
- [ ] Documentation update

#### Overview of change:

* Move `disabledIntervals` out of rule options. Rules are not responsible for disabling theirselves. Just filter the failures after the rule returns them.
  - While doing this, I removed `filterFailures` entirely, removing code that looked for duplicate failures. It turns out a few rules were returning duplicate failures, so I changed them directly.
* Don't expose `disabledIntervals` at all. Just have a `RuleDisabler` interface and a method for getting one from the disable comments in a source file.
  - Therefore, we can delete `IDisabledInterval`.

#### Is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on?

There were conflicting tests as to whether explicitly enabling a rule turned off in tslint.json would enable it. I chose that it would. If you don't want that, the `isExplicitlyEnabled` method could be removed.

#### CHANGELOG.md entry:

[no-log] change are internal and backwards compatible

— discussion —
@ajafff: To summarize both inline discussions:
`Linter` needs to be refactored. It should get the rule config only once in the constructor instead of every call to `Linter.lint`. We can then load all rules (even disabled ones to enable them later) upfront to save I/O.
We could / should also validate or parse the options for every rule (related: #1950) instead of doing this partially in some rule's `isEnabled` method. This needs to be done to ensure a rule is properly configured when enabled via comment.

@ajafff: Related, but no blocker for this PR: when applying fixes, the position of the disabledIntervals may no longer be correct. It needs to be refreshed after each rule that applied fixes.

@andy-hanson: In order to keep this PR small, I've removed `isExplicitlyEnabled`. Changing the Linter API can be done later.

@nchen63: it doesn't look like any unit tests hit enableDisableRules.ts

@andy-hanson: There is a black-box test `test/rules/_integration/enable-disable`.
It would be nice to have code coverage tests though.

@andy-hanson: Test failure fixed by #2691.

@andy-hanson: @nchen This was originally written during tslint 4.0. What is the schedule for new major tslint releases? It seemed to be much slower in the past but the gap from 4.0 to 5.0 was pretty small. If it will be more than a few months before the next major-version release I can add dummy implementations over the breaking changes as @ajaff mentioned. Otherwise I would be fine with waiting a little longer.

@nchen63: There isn't a major release scheduled. It's usually based on how many breaking changes are queued up

Share common http functionality between links and update apollo-link-batch-http
artifacts.body:
Share common http functionality between links and update apollo-link-batch-http This PR contains code to remove the logic shared across all http links from apollo-link-http and put it into a publicly accessible `apollo-link-http-common` module. This module is used by apollo-link-batch-http to have consistent behavior around errors and serialization. This PR also add the ability to change a query's batch with the `batchKey` constructor option. `batchKey` is a function that accepts an operation and returns a string key that uniquely identifies the batch it belongs in. These changes also modify the way that the fetch option and request body are created, found in the `createOptionsAndBody` method (CC @jaydenseric). The config precedence remains the same(least to greatest): default, link constructor, context. This PR found and fixes a bug in apollo-link-batch for multiple subscribers on a single request. Issues of multiple subscription calls(#298) are still present in apollo-link-http. Thanks for getting this started! @evans: I think we can go in a better direction here. @jbaxleyiii pointed out [this article](https://reactjs.org/blog/2017/12/15/improving-the-repository-infrastructure.html) in react's blog. The important part is that we can create a shared unpublished package that includes the functionality shared (fetch option construction and response parsing+error handling) across `apollo-link-http`, `apollo-link-batch-http`, and `apollo-link-upload`(+`apollo-link-batch-upload`?). This private package will be bundled into the source for each package individually, so each of the packages stay in sync. This is a much better solution for the link ecosystem, especially since the [currently proposed code](https://github.com/apollographql/apollo-link/pull/364/files/7d62c6e27ab14435b516a4b3f4e2c424cd9a0c1a) doesn't really do the right thing for batching(by uri with a `Map`) For further context on ^, the current situation is that uri can be generated from the each operation’s `context.uri` or the constructor’s `uri: Operation -> String`. The correct action is to respect these per operation uris and create a batch for each of them that are all fired off on the interval or send an individual batch when it hits `batchMax`. CC @jaydenseric @jaydenseric: For DX it would be best if there was one terminating link that does fetching. No need to consumers to change their dependencies just to turn on batching or begin uploading files. Less packages to maintain and version, and less documentation to maintain and learn. For this approach there is no need for seperate helpers. I'm not following why the one package idea is no longer feasible? If there has to be seperate packages, it would be better to publish a helpers package so it can benefit packages outside of the repo. @darren128: What's the status on this? @evans: @darren128 Thank you for the checkin! @evans: Yeah @jaydenseric had similar sentiments! I think that `batchLink.concat(httpLink)` would complicate the request interface and make visual debugging(dev tools tracing a request through the chain) more difficult.

Whether we add the batching behavior to link-http or keep it in link-batch-http is a philosophical question to answer. I'm fine with having the terminating(transport) links owning batching, since I hope that batching becomes a standard.
